# R749SPJ — Complete exact upper-triangle Walsh minimax phase diagram

**Date:** 2026-11-15. **Status:** AUTHOR_EXACT_NOT_REVIEWED. **Scope:** auxiliary sixteen-atom Walsh compatible-source probability laws, with scientific inputs frozen at awdawmip/enterprise-math@a72226e2430ffa4786321ac86e7f0c599d5f0389. Native X6, P000, signed-Port semantics and V29/V39 operator correspondence remain separate.

**Exact predecessors:** R749SPG zero-gap triangles, Draft PR #2431 at e985f1c8f8d7fe2a7ff2914b1835d68d5ef5b6fc; R749SPI upper-fiber homothety and diagonal gap, Draft PR #2438 at d349f175dc31d4ff3ef3c7699f0b4cc46fbf48c0; R749SPH positive-gap trapezoid, Draft PR #2435 at 717a2854c72b3f4e8c23c862cdd91ec229aa493a. The new calculation resolves the previously open anti-diagonal segment, then uses the exact homothety to determine the entire upper two-parameter triangle.

## 1. Model and the complete exact theorems

Let K be F_2^4, chi_m(k)=(-1)^{popcount(k&m)}, and

\[
p_{t,s,h,u,v,w,z}(k)=
\frac{1+t\chi_3(k)+s\chi_{12}(k)+h\chi_{15}(k)+u\chi_1(k)+v\chi_2(k)+w\chi_4(k)+z\chi_8(k)}{16}.
\]

Let F(t,s) consist of *all* such normalized nonnegative laws with coefficients t,s fixed, with total variation TV(p,q)=sum_k |p(k)-q(k)|/2. Let rho(t,s) be the minimax radius with arbitrary probability center, rho_cal(t,s) its center-constrained-to-F(t,s) analogue, and g=rho_cal-rho.

**Theorem A (complete anti-diagonal, all real parameters).** Put (t,s)=(r,1-r), 1/2<=r<=1. Then

\[
\rho(r,1-r)=
\begin{cases}
\tfrac12-\tfrac r5,&\tfrac12\le r\le\tfrac59,\\
\tfrac{1+r}{4},&\tfrac59\le r\le1;
\end{cases}
\]

\[
\rho_{\rm cal}(r,1-r)=
\begin{cases}
\tfrac{6-3r}{11},&\tfrac12\le r\le\tfrac8{15},\\
\tfrac25,&\tfrac8{15}\le r\le\tfrac35,\\
\tfrac{1+r}{4},&\tfrac35\le r\le1.
\end{cases}
\]

The gap is therefore

\[
g(r,1-r)=
\begin{cases}
(5-8r)/110,&\tfrac12\le r\le\tfrac8{15},\\
(2r-1)/10,&\tfrac8{15}\le r\le\tfrac59,\\
(3-5r)/20,&\tfrac59\le r\le\tfrac35,\\
0,&\tfrac35\le r\le1.
\end{cases}
\]

The bit-pair exchange gives the other half of the anti-diagonal, r<=1/2. Explicit exact values (rho,rho_cal,g) are (2/5,9/22,1/110) at r=1/2, (59/150,2/5,1/150) at r=8/15, (7/18,2/5,1/90) at r=5/9, and (2/5,2/5,0) at r=3/5. Adjacent formulas agree at every boundary.

**Theorem B (complete upper parameter triangle, all real parameters).** For 0<=t,s<=1 with t+s>=1, write M=max(t,s), m=min(t,s). The following four cases cover the domain, including their consistent shared boundaries.

| Region | Exact condition | Free radius rho | Calibrated radius rho_cal | Gap g |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| I | 8M-7m <= 1 | (8-5M-3m)/10 | (9-6M-3m)/11 | (2-5M+3m)/110 |
| II | 8M-7m >= 1 and 5M-4m <= 1 | (8-5M-3m)/10 | 2(2-M-m)/5 | (M-m)/10 |
| III | 5M-4m >= 1 and 3M-2m <= 1 | (3-M-2m)/4 | 2(2-M-m)/5 | (1-3M+2m)/20 |
| IV | 3M-2m >= 1 | (3-M-2m)/4 | (3-M-2m)/4 | 0 |

The exact zero-gap locus in the upper parameter triangle is Region IV. The diagonal t=s=r, r in [1/2,1], obeys g=(1-r)/55, matching R749SPI. At (t,s)=(1,1), the fiber is a singleton and all radii vanish. No native X6 observer correspondence is claimed.

## 2. Four-branch BRC and explicit minimax lower bounds

Write a=chi_3, b=chi_12, c=chi_1, d=chi_4. All sixteen atoms have the *retained sign* chart

\[
16p=M_{ab}+cU_a+dV_b,\quad
M_{ab}=1+ta+sb+hab,\quad
U_a=u+av,\quad V_b=w+bz.
\]

Nonnegativity is **equivalent** to M_ab >= |U_a|+|V_b| on the four sign blocks. The four translations in ker chi_3 intersect ker chi_12 preserve F(t,s) and TV. Symmetrizing an arbitrary center by this group cannot raise its maximal TV risk. The free center becomes a set of four nonnegative per-atom block values x_{--},x_{-+},x_{+-},x_{++} with 4 sum x = 1; a calibrated center becomes q_h=p_{r,1-r,h,0,0,0,0}.

For all r in [1/2,3/5], define compatible source families

\[
P_-(r)=p_{r,1-r,0,-r,-r,r-1,r-1},\quad
P_+(r)=p_{r,1-r,0,r,r,1-r,1-r},
\]
\[
P_a(r)=p_{r,1-r,2-2r,1-2r,1-2r,0,0}.
\]

Each is affine in r and is normalized and nonnegative at the two endpoints, so belongs to F(r,1-r) throughout the continuous interval.

Let E_A={7,11,13,14,15}, E_B={0,3,5,6,9,10,12,15} and E_C={3,7,11,13,14,15}. Direct sixteen-atom Walsh expansion yields

\[
\tfrac45 P_-(E_A)+\tfrac15 P_a(E_B)-\tfrac25=\tfrac12-\tfrac r5,
\quad \tfrac12 TV(P_-,P_+)=\tfrac{1+r}{4}.
\]

For a symmetrized arbitrary free center, (4/5)q(E_A)+(1/5)q(E_B)=2/5-(4/5)x_{--}. The TV event inequality TV(P,q)>=P(E)-q(E), the maximum-versus-weighted-average inequality, and x_{--}>=0 imply rho >= 1/2-r/5. The pair P_+,P_- gives the second lower bound rho >= (1+r)/4. Their maximum changes branch exactly at r=5/9.

For a calibrated center q_h, the same two sources give three **simultaneously valid** event inequalities:

\[
P_-(E_A)-q_h(E_A)=3/8+3h/16,
\]
\[
P_-(E_C)-q_h(E_C)=1/4+r/4+h/8,
\quad
P_a(E_B)-q_h(E_B)=1-r-h/2.
\]

The first and third intersect at h=(10-16r)/11, with value (6-3r)/11; the second and third intersect at h=6/5-2r, with value 2/5. Minimizing the maximum of these affine pairs over *all real h* yields rho_cal >= max{(6-3r)/11,2/5}, switching at r=8/15. Restricting h to the actual source fiber cannot lower this universal bound.

For r in [1/2,3/5], the following centers match those lower bounds:

\[
q_f(r)=p_{1,(5-8r)/5,(5-8r)/5,0,0,0,0},
\]
\[
q_c(r)=p_{r,1-r,h_c(r),0,0,0,0},\qquad
h_c(r)=
\begin{cases}
(10-16r)/11,&r\le8/15,\\
6/5-2r,&r\ge8/15.
\end{cases}
\]

The first is an unrestricted probability center; the second is in F(r,1-r). Both are affine on the indicated rational intervals, normalized and nonnegative at all endpoints, hence throughout. We prove their *universal* upper bounds by an exact full vertex census.

## 3. Complete 6D rational polytope certificate for all real r

The joint source polytope has variables (r,h,u,v,w,z), the sixteen atom nonnegativity facets, and the two rational r-endpoint inequalities. It is bounded since any Walsh coefficient of a probability law is an expectation of a sign and lies in [-1,1]. Every joint vertex is the intersection of six linearly independent active facets. Thus the exhaustive finite set of C(18,6)=18,564 six-facet bases includes every vertex on each interval, including any interior-projection vertices.

The accompanying standard-library exact checker uses integer Bareiss elimination, rational back substitution with Python Fraction, full feasibility checking of all 18 inequalities, and deduplication of complete rational vertices. At every distinct vertex it verifies source, free-center and calibrated-center normalizations and nonnegativity, and evaluates *exactly* both risk excesses:

\[
TV(p_x,q_f(r))-\rho_{\rm candidate}(r)\le0,\quad
TV(p_x,q_c(r))-\rho_{{\rm cal},\rm candidate}(r)\le0.
\]

Both are convex functions of the complete joint six variables, because TV is a sum of absolute values of affine forms, and the subtracted radii are affine on each chosen interval. Therefore their maxima over each compact polytope are attained at vertices, and the exhaustive results prove the upper bounds over **every real source and every real r** in the interval.

| r interval | Active bases | Nonsingular | Feasible bases (repetitions included) | Distinct rational vertices | Max free excess / max calibrated excess |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| [1/2,8/15] | 18,564 | 10,848 | 912 | 37 | 0 / 0 |
| [8/15,5/9] | 18,564 | 10,848 | 880 | 40 | 0 / 0 |
| [5/9,3/5] | 18,564 | 10,848 | 880 | 40 | 0 / 0 |
| Total | **55,692** | **32,544** | **2,672** | **117 phase-counted** | **0 / 0** |

The executable program additionally validates the exact source-event equations, nonnegative endpoints, total mass, source-bit exchange, and exact parameter projections. Its saved JSON reports PASS with full counts, tight-vertex counts and maximal excess zero; no numerical tolerance or float LP solver enters the certificate.

On the remainder [3/5,1], the previously proven R749SPG zero-gap triangle yields rho=rho_cal=(1+r)/4 exactly. Bit-pair exchange handles the reflected half of the anti-diagonal. These results complete Theorem A.

## 4. Complete upper-triangle extension by exact source-fiber homothety

For every real t,s in [0,1] with t+s>=1 and (t,s)!=(1,1), define

\[
\nu=t+s-1,\quad
\alpha=2-t-s>0,\quad
t'=(1-s)/\alpha,\quad s'=(1-t)/\alpha.
\]

Let P_star=p_{1,1,1,0,0,0,0}. The exact source-fiber identity from R749SPI is

\[
F(t,s)=\nu P_\star+\alpha F(t',s'),\quad t'+s'=1.
\]

For completeness, one direction follows directly by convex combination and matching Walsh coefficients. Conversely, let p be an arbitrary nonnegative source in F(t,s). In all three blocks except ++, p-nu P_star is nonnegative because P_star vanishes. In ++, M_{--}=h-nu>=0, |U_+|<=M_{+-} and |V_+|<=M_{-+}. The exact BRC identity

\[
M_{++}-4\nu-(M_{+-}+M_{-+})=3(h-\nu)\ge0
\]

then gives M_{++}-4nu>=|U_+|+|V_+|. Thus p-nu P_star is atomwise nonnegative, and its normalized ratio with alpha lies in F(t',s'). This proves the source-fiber equality for all real parameters.

The unrestricted TV center minimax on the probability simplex equals minimax on the entire affine sum-one hyperplane. Indeed, given an affine signed center q, let N=sum_i max(-q_i,0), q^+_i=max(q_i,0), and q'_i=q^+_i/(1+N); then q' is a probability center and ||p-q'||_1<=||p-q||_1 for *each* probability source p. The map q->nu P_star+alpha q is a bijection of this affine hyperplane and scales L1 distances exactly by alpha. For calibrated centers, this map bijects the two source fibers. Hence

\[
\rho(t,s)=\alpha\rho(t',s'),\quad
\rho_{\rm cal}(t,s)=\alpha\rho_{\rm cal}(t',s'),\quad
g(t,s)=\alpha g(t',s').
\]

For M=max(t,s),m=min(t,s), the larger anti-diagonal argument is r=(1-m)/alpha. The breakpoints r=8/15, 5/9, 3/5 are precisely the upper-triangle lines 8M-7m=1, 5M-4m=1 and 3M-2m=1. Multiplying Theorem A by alpha on each case and simplifying gives Theorem B. At (1,1) the source fiber P_star is a singleton and all three radii are zero. Thus the classification includes the entire closed upper triangle.

## 5. Reproduction, author verification and next step

Complete source: R749SPJ_ANTIDIAGONAL_FULL_PHASE_EXACT_CERT.py. Complete executed stdout: R749SPJ_ANTIDIAGONAL_FULL_PHASE_RESULTS.json. Run with Python 3 standard library:

    python3 R749SPJ_ANTIDIAGONAL_FULL_PHASE_EXACT_CERT.py > R749SPJ_ANTIDIAGONAL_FULL_PHASE_RESULTS.json

The script was actually executed using exact Python Fraction and integer Bareiss arithmetic, with 55,692 active sets and PASS on all three parameter subranges. The all-real theorem uses a **mathematically complete vertex census + convexity**, not extrapolation from finite parameter samples. The upper-homothety proof is algebraic and does not depend on finite sampling. R749SPG and R749SPI remain the explicitly pinned author-side scientific dependencies; independent mathematical review and formal source admission remain open.

**Next:** classify the lower parameter triangle t+s<1 using compatible-fiber decomposition or exact event duality, testing whether two-dimensional strictly positive-gap chambers occur outside the previously proved zero-gap subregions. Independently study provenance- and operation-preserving correspondence to native X6/V29/V39; retain signed sources and the locked P000 three-dimensional-slice semantics.
